key_insight: Co-designing partial fault tolerance with neutral-atom hardware could enable lower-overhead quantum simulation using a few thousand qubits at physical error rates near 10⁻³.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware pulse optimization and logical-circuit design can reduce resource costs without requiring fully fault-tolerant non-Clifford operations.
method: Identify and enhance favorable noise bias in ¹⁷¹Yb Rydberg gates through error-selective pulse optimization.
Model logical errors and evaluate surface-code implementations with circuit-level simulations.
Design periodic-boundary Fermi–Hubbard simulation circuits and compare partial versus full fault-tolerance resources.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show over 10× lower logical error than prior estimates, while resource estimates indicate roughly 10× lower state-injection depth than fully fault-tolerant gate synthesis.
watch_item: The projected benefits depend on achieving the modeled hardware noise characteristics; non-Clifford operations remain partially protected rather than fully fault tolerant.
paper_title: End-to-End Optimization of Partial Fault Tolerance in Neutral-Atom Arrays
